Strategic Framework | Element | Objective | Why it matters | |---------|-----------|----------------| | **Corridor Prioritisation** | Decide which routes to serve first | Resource optimisation, quickest ROI | | **Equipment Tiering** | Passive, powered, & solar‑powered solutions | Match road quality & electricity reliability | | **Seasonal Windowing** | Deliver during “cold windows” | Reduce the need for powered cooling | | **Governance** | Ministry of Health (MoH), customs, local partners | Regulatory compliance + institutional trust | | **Monitoring** | Real‑time IoT temperature & GPS | Reduce spoilage risk & prove accountability | | **Contingency** | Backup units, buffer inventory, reroute logic | Mitigate interruptions from traffic, power loss, weather | --- ## 2. Corridor Mapping & Constraints | Corridor | West Africa | East Africa | Key Constraints | |----------|-------------|-------------|-----------------| | **Lagos – Accra (West)** | Highway: 200 km, 2‑lane, pothole‑heavy | Highway: 600 km, 2‑lane, moderate potholes | Road quality **+** customs dwell 24–48 h | | **Accra – Dakar (West)** | 2000 km, 1‑lane, occasional river crossings | 3000 km, 4‑lane segments, heavy traffic | Road quality **** + long customs windows | | **Dakar – Bamako (West)** | 600 km, semi‑paved, 2‑lane | 2000 km, 1‑lane, high traffic | Road quality + *no* reliable electricity at rest stops | | **Addis Ababa – Nairobi (East)** | 1400 km, 2‑lane, high altitude | 2000 km, 2‑lane, seasonal rains | Road quality **+** occasional flooding, customs delays | | **Kigali – Kampala (East)** | 400 km, 2‑lane, moderate potholes | 500 km, 2‑lane, moderate potholes | Road quality **+** limited last‑mile infrastructure | | **Mombasa – Harare (East)** | 2000 km, 2‑lane, poor gravel sections | 2500 km, 2‑lane, heavy traffic & seasonal rains | Road quality **+** electricity reliability ** (bad)** | ### Institutional & Physical Constraints Summarised | Factor | West Africa | East Africa | |--------|-------------|-------------| | **Road Quality** | Variable 1‑2 lanes, many potholes | Mostly 2‑lane gravel, frequent floods | | **Customs** | 24–48 h dwell in many border towns | 12–24 h, sometimes >48 h | | **Electricity** | Rare at rest stops, low voltage, unsystematic | Spotty in rural areas, no grid in remote villages | | **Last‑mile** | Mostly hand‑off to local health centre, limited transport | Mixed: village vans, mobile vans, motorbike couriers | | **Seasonality** | Dry season 3–4 a.m.–7 p.m. cooler | Wet season 12–6 p.m. cooler, high humidity | --- ## 3. Equipment Selection Matrix | Use‑Case | Equipment | Specs | Rationale | Typical Cost (USD) | |----------|-----------|-------|-----------|--------------------| | **Long‑haul corridor (≥ 600 km)** | **Truck‑mounted active refrigeration unit (IRU, 4 °C ± 0.5)** | 3‑5 °C set point, 24 h power, battery backup | Keeps vaccines within 2 °C–8 °C during transit | $10 k–$15 k per unit | | **Moderate‐length corridors → 2–4 h** | **Passive thermal tank (PCM + ice packs) with 72 h capacity** | Phase‑change material (4 °C), pre‑cooled | No power needed, fits short road dwell | $1–$1.5 k per unit | | **Last‑mile (≤ 50 km)** | **Solar‑powered mobile cold storage**

Corridor Sequencing & Seasonal Planning | Activity | Year‑1 (Q1–Q4) | Year‑2 (Q1–Q4) | |----------|----------------|----------------| | **Pilot Corridors** | **Lagos – Accra** (West) & **Addis – Nairobi** (East) | + **Dakar – Bamako** (West) | | **Infrastructure Build‑out** | Solar arrays + battery storage at key rest stops (Lagos–Accra, Addis) | Expand thermal tank fleet (Bamako) | | **Scaling** | Add **Accra – Dakar** (West), **Kigali – Kampala** (East) | Add **Mombasa–Harare** (East) | | **Seasonally Optimised Dispatch** | Dry season (Mar–Jun) – use passive tanks for north‑south runs; wet season – active IRUs for high‑risk routes | Continue cyclical adaptation | ### Scheduling Logic 1. **Cold Window Analysis** – Use historical temperature data to identify 6‑hour “night‑time” windows. 2. **Road Dwell Calculation** – Estimate dwell time + transit time → choose passive vs active. 3. **Customs Pre‑Clearance** – Whenever possible, arrange *paper‑free* checks (e.g., via MoH digital customs). 4. **Buffer Time Allocation** – Add 10 % of expected travel time as contingency buffer, especially for wet season. --- ## 5. Load vaccines in pre‑cools at 1 °C. 2. Verify all temperature loggers and backup power. 3. Route with predicted dwell ≤ 4 h (if passive). 4. Monitor GPS & temperature logs in real‑time. 5. Update MoH & local partners within 2 h if deviation > 2 °C. --- ## 6. Monitoring, Reporting & Continuous Improvement | Tool & Metric | Frequency | Owner | |---------------|-----------|-------| | **IoT Dashboard** – avg temp, max temp, GPS | Live | Ops & Compliance | | **Monthly KPI Report** – % trips within temperature window | Monthly | Analytics | | **Quarterly Spoilage Audit** – Spoilage incidents, root‑cause | Quarterly | QA/Quality | | **Feedback Loop** – Health centre satisfaction survey | Bi‑annual | CS | | **Seasonal Update** – Shift plans based on climate trends | Quarterly | Ops | - All data should feed into a **Real‑time Compliance Portal** accessible to MoH, partners, and auditors. - Leverage **Machine‑Learning** to predict temperature excursions before they occur (anomaly detection on temperature vs route). --- ## 7. Implementation Roadmap (18 Months) | Phase | Key Activities | Deliverables | |-------|----------------|--------------| | **0–3 mo** | Finalise equipment procurement, build SOPs, set up IoT fleet | Equipment spec sheet, SOP manual | | **4–6 mo** | Pilot runs on Lagos–Accra & Addis–Nairobi; monitor, refine routing | Pilot KPI report, risk register | | **7–12 mo** | Deploy additional corridors (Accra–Dakar, Bamako–Dakar) | Full routing database, temperature logs | | **13–18 mo** | Expand last‑mile solar units to key health centres; roll‑out monitoring dashboard | Dashboard launch, health‑centre training | | **Post‑18 mo** | Continuous optimization; scale to all corridors | Full network coverage, KPI baseline | --- ## 8. Key Performance Indicators (for 2026 launch) | KPI | Target | Measurement Tool | |-----|--------|------------------| | **Temperature Compliance** | ≥ 99 % of shipments 2 °C–8 °C | IoT dashboard | | **Delivery on Time** | ≥ 95 % arrivals within scheduled window | GPS & time‑stamp logs | | **Spoilage Rate** | < 0.5 % of vaccine doses | QA audit | | **Customer Satisfaction** | ≥ 9/10 | CSAT survey | | **Operational Cost per Dose** | < $1.50 | Finance KPIs | --- ## 9. Governance & Partnerships | Role | Responsibility | Partners | |------|----------------|----------| | **Country Lead (MoH liaison)** | Approve routes, customs clearance | MoH, DHS | | **Legal/Compliance** | Draft MoU, ensure GDPR/COVID‑19 alignment | Local counsel | | **Supply Chain Ops** | Fleet scheduling, route optimization | Transport firms, local couriers | | **Technical Ops** | Fleet maintenance & IoT integration | Carrier tech, local ICT firms | | **Quality Assurance** | Spoilage audits, ISO 13485 compliance | ISO auditors, vaccine manufacturer | *Stakeholder Map* – Include local health offices, customs brokers, energy providers (for solar installs), and regional logistics unions. --- ## 10. Sustainability Considerations - **Renewable Energy** – Solar arrays at rest stops reduce reliance on diesel. - **Carbon‑Offset** – Use fuel‑efficient trucks (Euro 6) and integrate CO₂‑offset programs. - **Community Empowerment** – Train local health workers in cold‑chain handling, create micro‑enterprise opportunities (e.g., local van operators) with subsidised cold units. --- ## Summary - **Prioritise corridors** based on road quality, customs time, and last‑mile capacity. - **Match equipment**: Active IRUs for long, power‑stressed routes; passive PCMs for short, predictable legs; solar units for electricity‑poor last‑mile. - **Sequence deliveries** around seasonal temperature windows and predicted dwell times. - **Embed real‑time monitoring** and rapid‑swap contingency to keep spoilage below 0.5 %. - **Governance, training, & local partnerships** ensure regulatory compliance and institutional trust. Adopting this blueprint will enable a resilient, compliant, and low‑churn cold‑chain program across Africa’s diverse logistical landscape.
